name: Irrigation and sprinkler installer

pf.license.need: if: an irrigation contractor license or registration for the company, and a license or certificate for each person who designs, installs or tests, where the state's form requires them (some states license irrigation on its own, some under a landscape or plumbing license, some not at all)
ask: The company's irrigation license or registration number, and its class
For each irrigator who designs or installs, their license number, where the state's form asks
For each backflow tester, their test certificate and its number (a device that protects the drinking water is tested by a certified tester)
General liability insurance; workers' comp where the business has employees
A bond, where the state's form asks for one
pf.license.holder: The business holds the company license. A licensed irrigator signs the design and the permit where the rules ask. A certified tester signs each backflow test.
pf.license.check: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, insurance or registration (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
blocks: No irrigation work goes live until the company's license checks out, where one is required
A backflow test is offered only by a tester whose certificate the business gives
A job over the license's size limit is never offered or quoted: the owner is told why
pf.license.renewals: License, certificate, insurance and bond dates kept; reminded 30 days out; a lapse pauses that person's bookings
pf.license.water_district: A new backflow device or a test may be filed with the water district, where the rules ask; the tester files it
pf.license.background: Background checks only where the state's form asks
pf.license.shop: The shop: a registration where the state's form asks; selling or setting up a controller needs no license

pf.services.pattern: Seasonal service at the home at a set price, a visit to look and then a quote for a repair, and a design visit then a contract for a new system

B.service: Fall winterization (blow the water out of the lines before the first hard freeze)
B.price: $179; each zone over 8 is $15 (the example business's own prices)
B.place: at the customer's place; nobody needs to be home with a gate code
B.before: a card saved for the $89 trip fee
B.after: the saved card is charged when the tech texts DONE

B.service: Spring start-up and check (turn the water on, run every zone, adjust heads, set the controller)
B.price: $150 a visit, a plan customer's price (the yearly plan: a start-up in spring, a winterization in fall, each paid in full when booked)
B.place: at the customer's place; nobody needs to be home with a gate code

B.service: Sprinkler repair (broken heads, a leaking valve, a pipe leak, wiring)
B.price: only the $89 trip fee is promised, counted toward the repair (example: $245)
B.before: a card saved for the $89 trip fee
B.after: the saved card is charged when the tech texts DONE

B.service: Extra zone, drip line or smart controller (priced from photos and a yard sketch)
B.price: the quote (the example: $640; over $500, Sam OKs it)
B.length: half a day to a day
B.before: the utility locate first if anything is dug; then a 25% deposit once the quote is OK'd

B.service: New sprinkler system (design visit, then a written quote and a contract)
B.price: its own quote (the example: $2,400 for a back lawn, billed in three stages)
B.before: a deposit only after the contract is signed; the utility locate and any permit first
B.after: stage bills, the last after the backflow test and the zone walk-through

B.service: System audit and report (a flow and coverage check, for a water bill or a sale)
B.before: nothing, or a card saved for the $89 trip fee
B.after: the bill; the report comes the same day or the next

B.service: Backflow test and certificate (the yearly test of the device that protects the drinking water)
B.price: $95, with the certificate filed where the water district asks
B.note: Only a certified tester. A device that fails is repaired or replaced, then retested.

B.price: free; a written quote from the photos Alex sends, for small jobs
B.place: by text or the secure page; nobody comes
B.after: nothing more; Alex can book a visit from the quote

B.note: Goes on quoted repairs; not booked alone

A.place: at the shop; or at the customer's home for $75, paid in full when booked
A.before: a card saved for the $20 missed-consult fee

A.place: at the shop; the customer brings the controller and stays while it is programmed

A.note: The customer brings an old head; the tech matches the nozzle and spray pattern

A.service: Watering schedule session (a schedule by zone that follows the water district's rules)
A.price: $55, 60 minutes; counts toward a new system if Alex signs with Lee Irrigation

A.service: Full irrigation plan (design, zone map, parts list)
A.before: a card saved for the $40 fee (over 2 hours), or a $40 deposit

A.price kind: priced from the customer's photos and a yard sketch
A.price: the quote (the example: $90); Sam OKs each one

A.note: The consultant sees the old controller and the zone count first

pf.services.capacity: One tech or consultant per booking; one crew per install, up to 3 days; a trench day needs two people. The shop's layout table is saved with long sessions.
pf.services.skills each needs: Winterization and start-up: any tech. Repairs: a tech cleared for valves and wiring. Design and installs: a licensed irrigator where the state asks. Backflow tests: a certified tester.
pf.services.nobody home: Winterization and start-up: nobody needs to be home with a gate code; a start photo and an end photo. A repair or a design visit: an adult is home. Never left with a child.
pf.services.online: No video consult: designs use the yard, the photos and the zone map
pf.services.extras: Travel inside the service area only (the example: 25 miles). Parts at the owner's price, shown on the quote. No tax line unless the owner sets a rate. A system fed by a well pump: the pump and its wiring are an electrician's job, not touched here.

before times (they set the price, length: What is it: a winterization, a start-up, a repair, a backflow test or a new system or zone?
How many zones does the system have, if you know?
What feeds it: city water, a well or a rainwater tank?
Is anything broken or leaking now?
after a time is picked: Who will be home: the customer, or another adult (their name and mobile go on the secure page)
Gate, dog and where the controller and the water shut-off are
Do you own the home or rent? (the owner signs any new system)
Is the home in an owners' association? (some need approval for a new system)
only on the secure page: Photos of the yard, the controller and the backflow device
A sketch of the yard, for a new system
pf.questions.who may book: An adult. A renter may book a winterization, a start-up or a repair with the owner's OK; the owner signs a new system. A business or a property manager books as an organization.
shop: What the customer wants: a plan, a controller setup, a nozzle match
Photos of the yard and the old controller (optional)

stops the booking.words: A gas smell, sparks, smoke or a burning smell from the controller or an outlet; a gas or power line hit while digging
stops the booking.says: Leave the area now and keep everyone away. Once outside, call 911 and the gas or power company.
stops the booking.booking: No booking until the gas or power company clears it.

stops the booking.words: Water reaching the electrical panel, or standing water at outlets with the power on
stops the booking.says: Stay out of the water. Don't touch the panel or any outlet. If it is safe to reach, switch off the main breaker from a dry spot; otherwise leave and call 911.

safety steps, then the booking goes on,.words: Water spraying or flooding from a broken head, pipe or valve
safety steps, then the booking goes on,.says: Shut off the irrigation water at its shut-off valve if you can reach it safely. Keep away from wet outlets and the controller.
safety steps, then the booking goes on,.booking: Goes on, marked urgent; the soonest time is offered first.

safety steps, then the booking goes on,.words: The backflow device leaking or spraying, or odd-tasting or odd-smelling drinking water after the system ran
safety steps, then the booking goes on,.says: Shut off the irrigation water if it's safe. Don't run the system. Call the water company about the drinking water.

pf.safety.business_line: Questions about whether the drinking water is safe, or about the electrical panel, go to the business's own line
pf.safety.never: Customers are told never to dig near a marked line, and never to work on the controller's wiring from the house panel

pf.first_steps.at the start of the visit: A start-up begins with a pressure check at the backflow device and the main valve: passed, the zones run; a leak or a weak valve is priced first and needs the customer's yes
pf.first_steps.before the first visit: A new system or an extra zone waits for the utility locate (buried lines marked) before any digging, about 3 days; the first open times start after that. The permit, where the rules ask, is pulled by the license holder.
prep: Leave the gate unlocked or give the code on the secure page, and keep the controller, the valve boxes and the shut-off clear
For a start-up or a repair, an adult home if the controller is inside
For a new system, mark where pets, a septic tank and any private lines are, and don't dig before the locate
shop prep: Bring the old controller and photos of the yard, if you have them
Bring an old head for a nozzle match

pf.visit.check_in: At the home: the check-in code at the door, or a start photo from the crew where nobody is home. At the shop: the code at the counter.
pf.visit.at_the_visit: A winterization blows the water out of every zone with compressed air and drains the backflow device. A start-up turns the water on, runs every zone, and adjusts the heads and the controller. A leak or a broken part is shown and priced before it is fixed.
pf.visit.changes: A broken head, a weak valve or a leak found at a visit is priced first and needs the customer's yes. Work done is billed; work declined is not.
pf.visit.install_day: Lines marked, trench opened and closed the same day, ruts raked, a zone walk-through and the backflow test before the last stage
pf.visit.outside_checks: The backflow test and certificate, and a permit inspection where the permit requires one
pf.visit.done: Every zone shown running, the controller set, then DONE
pf.visit.shop done: DONE after the consult, with the plan saved; or READY for a controller setup
pf.visit.before photos: The controller, the backflow device and any broken head, with the zone number

pf.money.visit: A winterization or a repair: a card is saved for the $89 trip fee, and charged when the tech texts DONE. The $89 is owed after a no to a repair price and counts toward the repair.
pf.money.yearly plan: A yearly plan is a start-up in spring and a winterization in fall at $150 a visit, each paid in full when booked; each visit is booked and paid like a single one.
pf.money.new system: A new system is a design visit, then a written quote and a contract; a deposit only after signing, stage bills, the last after the backflow test. The deposit cap comes from the state's form.
pf.money.extra zone: An extra zone priced from photos takes a 25% deposit once the quote is OK'd, and the rest on the bill
pf.money.rosfield_fee: Rosfield's $2 follows the plug-in's choice at sign-up; counted at the first check-in or at DONE
pf.money.big_bills: Bank transfer through the company's own Stripe, for bills over the owner's amount (the example: $500); paid once it clears
pf.money.tax: Tax on parts and labor follows the state's form
pf.money.shop: A design consult's $35 is the shop's; a watering schedule session is paid in full when booked and counts toward a new system; a $20 fee on a consult only after Sam OKs it

never_in_texts: The street address (the secure page has it)
Contract, change-order and permit papers (secure page only, with a copy by email)
pf.messages.minors: Never booked by a minor; a child at home never lets the crew in

pf.staff.roles: Irrigation techs and crew leads (Bram, Selin): winterizations, start-ups, repairs and installs. Shop consultants (Noor, Kit).
pf.staff.licenses: A licensed irrigator designs and signs a new system where the state asks; a certified tester signs each backflow test; both are checked before they are named on a job
pf.staff.who_oks: Sam OKs quotes over $500; Pat may OK them too, and Sam's answer wins
pf.staff.stand_in: Another tech may take a winterization or a start-up; a design or an install keeps its licensed irrigator unless Sam moves it
pf.staff.on_call: None: every job is booked ahead
pf.staff.digging: A crew never digs before the utility locate; a marked line in the way stops that trench

pf.rules.contract: A written contract for a new system or an extra zone above the plug-in's amount (the example: $500), signed by everyone on title before any money
pf.rules.cancel_window: A cancel window after signing, where the state's rules give one. Work and orders wait for it.
pf.rules.locate: The utility locate before any digging; the license holder calls for it, never the customer
pf.rules.permits: A new system: pulled by the license holder in the business's name, where the rules require one
pf.rules.backflow: A new system gets a backflow device that is tested before the last stage; the test is filed where the water district asks
pf.rules.water_rules: The controller is set to the water district's rules on watering days and hours, where they apply
pf.rules.change_orders: Written and signed by both before added work, past what the contract already OK'd
pf.rules.warranty: 1 year on a new system's parts and labor, 90 days on a repair (the example's)
pf.rules.records: The zone count, the controller model and the last test date are kept for the next visit; 7 years

pf.edges.weather: A winterization moves up when a hard freeze is forecast, and a start-up waits until after the last hard freeze; no digging in frozen or soaked ground. A weather move never costs the customer.
pf.edges.freeze_damage: A cracked pipe or head found at a start-up is priced first; it is the customer's yes, not the tech's choice
pf.edges.backflow_fails: A device that fails its test is repaired or replaced, then tested again; the certificate waits, and the last stage waits
pf.edges.buried_line: A marked or unmarked line in the way stops that trench; the crew leaves the area, the customer gets a written note, and the utility comes first
pf.edges.well_pump: A system fed by a well pump: the pump, its wiring and its panel are an electrician's job; the tech never works on them
pf.edges.water_rules: A city's watering days or bans: the schedule follows them; the tech does not run zones on a banned day
pf.edges.nobody_home: Winterizations and start-ups: start and end photos; repairs and design visits: an adult is home
pf.edges.over_license_limit: Not offered, and the owner is told why
pf.edges.other: All other edge cases are handled the generic way

notes:
New profession on the REDESIGN 2 master (batch P4, Tue Oct 27 2026), built from lawn (refitted that morning, check-prof 0/0). Why lawn: irrigation is a set seasonal service at the home (a winterization in fall, a start-up in spring, nobody home with a gate code, a card saved and charged at DONE), with repairs priced at the visit and a new system as a project. Unlike lawn: no weekly plan, no sprays or neighbor notices, no mower-shop drop-off; the second side is a sprinkler shop where Alex stays (design consults, controller setup), built like a showroom.
Flow B main path (list|card|card): a $179 fall winterization of an 8-zone system at 14 Orchard Way, Thu Oct 22, 8-10am with Bram, before the first freeze (the master's October calendar). A card is saved for the $89 trip fee and charged $179 when Bram texts DONE. Other B paths: list|none|bill (a returning customer), list|full|none (the spring start-up, $150 paid in full when booked: the yearly plan is a start-up in spring and a winterization in fall, each visit paid like a single one), photos|deposit|bill (an extra zone, drip line or smart controller, $640 from photos and a yard sketch, over $500 so Sam OKs it, 25% deposit $160), visit|card|card (a sprinkler repair priced at the visit: valve $165 + heads $80 = $245; only the $89 trip fee is promised and counts toward the repair). The system audit and report ($199) is added at a visit and paid with the rest; the backflow test ($95) is booked by a certified tester.
A new system is the master's estimate path (B8-93 '1 Signs the contract' -> B8-62 -> B8-63 start payment -> B8-78 cancel window, switch cancelright on in B only -> B9-21 stage bills), with Harper J.'s $2,400 back-lawn system in three stages ($800 / $800 when the lines are laid / $800 after the backflow test). Own steps: B8-x07 and B8-x08 Sam calls for the utility locate and files the permit (Wed Oct 28, due before Mon Nov 2; late: new days Mon Nov 9 or Tue Nov 10, no fee); B8-x11 the crew starts and opens the trench; B8-x12 and B8-x13 the last day: the backflow device is tested and every zone is run (a pass is certified and filed; a fail is fixed and retested, and the last stage waits). The first-step mechanism carries two real rules: a new system or an extra zone waits for the utility locate (B4-97 lead time), and a start-up begins with a pressure check at the backflow device (B8-89 / B8-90).
Stop words: a gas smell, sparks, smoke or a burning smell from the controller or an outlet, a gas or power line hit while digging, water reaching the breaker panel or standing at powered outlets. Water spraying from a broken head or pipe, and a backflow device leaking or odd drinking water, get the safety steps and the booking goes on, marked urgent. B8-30's hazard is a marked gas line right where the trench goes (stop that trench, written note, the gas company first). A crew never digs before the locate. A system fed by a well pump: the pump and its wiring are an electrician's job.
Licenses: an irrigation license or registration at the company, a license for each irrigator who designs or installs and a certificate for each backflow tester, where the state's form asks (S1-60 keeps 'A license' and S2-28 keeps 'Yes, each one'); a certified tester signs each backflow test, filed where the water district asks. No state, city or law is named; license numbers use the EX- format. Not booked: a minor; a visit with no adult home when the visit needs one; a renter signing a new system without the owner; a job over the license limit.
Money: the $89 is the trip fee, the late-cancel and no-show fee, owed after a no to a repair price. Nothing is taken before a new system's contract is signed by everyone; deposits only after signing (or 25% on an extra zone once the quote is OK'd); the last stage after the backflow test. No tip line (S1-21's tip row is paired out). Added work is paid with the rest at the visit (D91). The $89 fee also sits on the $179 winterization (97 master steps hard-code $89); the owner may set a smaller fee. Warranty: 90 days on a repair, 1 year on a new system (the example's).
Flow A is the sprinkler shop (Lee Sprinkler Shop, Sam's second company, consultants Noor and Kit; the customer stays): design consult $35 (card saved for the $20 missed-consult fee; or at home for $75), controller setup session $40, nozzle match $25, zone map print $20, a quick chat (free), a watering schedule session $55 paid in full, a full irrigation plan $140 with a $40 deposit, a photo zone plan $90 (Sam OKs), a smart controller match priced at the shop after the $25 consult.
